subcategories.label: Faculty or staff business travel
subcategories.description: Any trip for a current employee — conference, audition panel, research, or other business purpose.

accounts.why: Use for any travel by a current Conservatory employee — airfare, hotel, conference registration, meals while traveling, or ground transportation.

subcategories.label: Recruiting a job candidate
subcategories.description: Travel reimbursement or direct booking for a faculty or staff candidate visiting campus.

accounts.why: Use for all travel expenses related to bringing a job candidate to campus for an interview or audition — airfare, hotel, meals, and ground transportation.
examples: Candidate airfare for faculty search visit
Candidate meal during campus interview day

subcategories.label: Training or professional development (no travel)
subcategories.description: Registration fees for workshops, online courses, or certifications — no travel component.

accounts.why: Use for professional development that doesn't involve travel — webinar fees, online certification programs, or local workshop registration.

subcategories.label: Fuel for a university vehicle or van
subcategories.description: Gas or fuel purchases for a Conservatory or university-owned vehicle.

accounts.why: Use when purchasing fuel for a university-owned or rented vehicle used for Conservatory business.
examples: Gas for van transporting students to performance
Gas station charge on university card for touring trip

subcategories.label: Benefit-eligible employee (regular staff position)
subcategories.description: A regular full-time or part-time staff employee who receives benefits.

accounts.why: Use for wages and salary paid to benefit-eligible staff employees — those in regular positions that include health insurance, retirement, and other benefits.

subcategories.label: Part-time or temporary staff (no benefits)
subcategories.description: Temporary or part-time employees who are not benefit-eligible.

accounts.why: Use for wages paid to non-benefit-eligible employees — part-time, temporary, or casual workers hired for operational or production support.

subcategories.label: Student employee (non-academic role)
subcategories.description: A student hired in an operational or administrative role (not academic/instructional work).

accounts.why: Use for student employees working in operational, administrative, or support roles — not for accompanist or curricular work.

subcategories.label: Academic worker — accompanist or curricular support
subcategories.description: A student or non-faculty worker in an academic or instructional role.

accounts.why: Use for academic workers who are not faculty — primarily student accompanists and students in curricular support roles like ensemble conducting.
examples: Student accompanist for lessons or ensemble
Student conducting an ensemble as part of curriculum

subcategories.label: Overtime pay
subcategories.description: Overtime wages for an hourly employee.

accounts.why: Use specifically for overtime pay — hours worked beyond the standard workweek for hourly employees.
examples: Production crew overtime during tech week
Staff overtime for a major event

subcategories.label: General or office supplies
subcategories.description: Everyday consumable supplies for office, administrative, or operational use.

accounts.why: Use for general consumable supplies that don't fit a more specific category — office materials, production consumables, or general operational supplies.
examples: Gaffer tape, cable ties, consumable production materials

subcategories.label: Instructional or academic materials
subcategories.description: Supplies used directly in teaching — scores, method books, classroom materials.

accounts.why: Use for materials directly supporting instruction or curriculum — not equipment, not general office supplies.
examples: Method books or textbooks for a course

subcategories.label: Shop, production, or technical supplies
subcategories.description: Materials used in production shops — scenic, costume, lighting, or sound supplies.

accounts.why: Use for consumable materials used in production shops or technical departments — scenic materials, hardware, costume consumables, and similar.
examples: Lumber and hardware for scenic construction
Cable, connectors, or hardware for sound/lighting

subcategories.label: Recruiting or audition materials
subcategories.description: Supplies specifically for student recruitment or audition events.

accounts.why: Use for supplies specifically purchased for student recruitment or audition days — distinct from general marketing or office supplies.
examples: Giveaways or handouts for prospective students

subcategories.label: Computer, tablet, or peripheral device
subcategories.description: Hardware purchase under $5,000.

accounts.why: Use for computers, laptops, tablets, or peripherals (keyboard, monitor, etc.) that cost less than $5,000.

subcategories.label: Software license or subscription
subcategories.description: Software purchase, license, or recurring digital subscription.

accounts.why: Use for software purchases, annual license renewals, and digital subscriptions under $5,000.

subcategories.label: Equipment purchase under $5,000
subcategories.description: Non-computer equipment — instruments, audio/visual gear, studio equipment.

accounts.why: Use for equipment purchases that are not computers and cost less than $5,000.

subcategories.label: Equipment purchase $5,000 or more
subcategories.description: Capital equipment purchase at or above the $5,000 threshold.

accounts.why: Use for any single equipment purchase at or above $5,000 — these are capitalized and tracked as university assets.

subcategories.label: Furniture or fixtures
subcategories.description: Desks, chairs, shelving, or other furniture under $5,000.

accounts.why: Use for furniture and fixture purchases under $5,000 — office furniture, studio furniture, or production fixtures.

subcategories.label: Equipment rental or lease
subcategories.description: Short-term or one-time equipment rental — not an automated recurring lease.

accounts.why: Use for renting or leasing equipment on a one-time or short-term basis.
examples: Audio equipment rental for a concert

subcategories.label: IT services or computing support
subcategories.description: Technology services, support contracts, or computing-related expenses that aren't hardware or software purchases.

accounts.why: Use for IT service charges, computing support, or technology-related expenses that aren't a discrete hardware or software purchase.

subcategories.label: Guest artist, clinician, or external consultant
subcategories.description: Honorarium or fee for an outside individual providing professional services.

accounts.why: Use for honoraria, fees, and payments to external individuals or businesses for professional services — guest artists, clinicians, consultants, royalties, and licensing fees.
examples: Consulting fee for an external professional

subcategories.label: Contracted performer or production specialist
subcategories.description: A contracted individual or company providing performance or production services.

accounts.why: Use for contracted performers, technicians, or production specialists engaged through a formal contract or service agreement.
examples: Piano technician or instrument repair specialist
Contracted stage crew or production specialist

subcategories.label: Service from another UM department (internal)
subcategories.description: Charges from another university department or UM System unit.

accounts.why: Use for interdepartmental charges — services billed from one UM unit to another.
examples: UMKC facilities or AV services charge
University Police or event security through campus

subcategories.label: External security services
subcategories.description: Security services from an outside vendor (not UM campus police).

accounts.why: Use for external security vendor charges for events or facilities.
examples: Event security contractor for a performance
External security services for a large event

subcategories.label: Printing or copying
subcategories.description: Printed materials — programs, flyers, reports, photocopies.

accounts.why: Use for printing and copying charges — programs, posters, promotional materials, or documents.

subcategories.label: Advertising or marketing
subcategories.description: Paid placement — digital ads, print ads, or promotional campaigns.

accounts.why: Use for paid advertising placements and marketing campaigns — digital, print, or broadcast.

subcategories.label: Food for a meeting, reception, or event
subcategories.description: Catering or food purchased for a university business purpose.

accounts.why: Use for food and beverage purchased for meetings, receptions, audition days, or university events with a documented business purpose.
examples: Food for a board or advisory committee meeting

subcategories.label: Postage, shipping, or delivery
subcategories.description: Mailing or shipping charges.

accounts.why: Use for postage and shipping — mailing recruitment materials, shipping equipment, or any delivery charges.

subcategories.label: Phone or communications services
subcategories.description: Telephone, mobile, or communications service charges.

accounts.why: Use for recurring or one-time phone and communications charges.

subcategories.label: Renting a space or venue
subcategories.description: Rental of a space or facility for a Conservatory event or activity.

accounts.why: Use for renting or leasing a venue, rehearsal space, or facility.

subcategories.label: Facilities charges or building services
subcategories.description: Charges for building-related services, maintenance, or facility use fees.

accounts.why: Use for miscellaneous facility-related charges under $5,000 that don't fit a more specific category.

subcategories.label: Equipment repair or maintenance
subcategories.description: Repair or maintenance of equipment — instruments, audio gear, etc.

accounts.why: Use for repairing or maintaining equipment — instruments, audio/visual equipment, or other non-capital items.
examples: Instrument repair (bow rehair, pad replacement, etc.)

subcategories.label: Building repair or maintenance
subcategories.description: Repairs, maintenance, or minor renovation to a building or facility.

accounts.why: Use for non-capital building maintenance and repair work.

subcategories.label: Minor renovation or facility improvement
subcategories.description: Small renovation or improvement project that doesn't meet the capital threshold.

accounts.why: Use for renovation or rehabilitation work on a facility that falls below the capital project threshold.
examples: Flooring replacement in a rehearsal room

subcategories.label: Insurance
subcategories.description: Insurance premiums or coverage charges.

accounts.why: Use for insurance premiums and coverage charges — event liability, instrument insurance, or similar.

subcategories.label: Dues or membership fees
subcategories.description: Annual dues or membership fees for a professional organization.

accounts.why: Use for annual dues or membership fees paid to professional organizations, accrediting bodies, or associations.
examples: NAfME, CMS, or other professional membership

subcategories.label: Professional development or training
subcategories.description: Registration for a workshop, seminar, or training program.

accounts.why: Use for professional development registration fees — workshops, online training, certifications, and seminars.
